description: A six-panel composite of cross-sectional SEM micrographs of crack-propagation zones; in every panel the upper edge is black (fracture surface / outside the specimen) and the grey field contains secondary-phase particles, fine striated twins and sparse round pores. (a) S1000, 10 µm scale bar: orange dashed outlines trace connected micropores/crack segments along grain boundaries and a white dashed box marks the area magnified in (b). (b) S1000, 5 µm: two white circles with arrows label "Cr7C3" particles sitting on grain boundaries. (c) S1050, 10 µm: a red dashed line labelled "Straight cracking" follows the near-surface crack, yellow dashed arrows labelled "Across the twins" and a white arrow labelled "Crack deflection" mark the path, plus an orange dashed outline and a white dashed box. (d) S1050, 5 µm: yellow dashed lines labelled "Across the twins" run along near-vertical twin boundaries. (e) MHT, 20 µm: low-magnification overview with only sparse round pores and a white dashed box. (f) MHT, 10 µm: a red dashed line labelled "Zigzag cracking", a white arrow labelled "Crack deflection" and yellow dashed lines labelled "Across the twins". The sequence therefore documents progressively increasing crack-path tortuosity: straight intergranular cracking in S1000 (pinned by Cr7C3), deflection along special boundaries/twins in S1050, and constant cross-boundary zigzag cracking in MHT.

observations.observation: Six SEM micrographs of cross-sectional crack-propagation regions are arranged as three pairs: (a, b) S1000, (c, d) S1050 and (e, f) MHT, with scale bars of 10 and 5 µm (S1000), 10 and 5 µm (S1050) and 20 and 10 µm (MHT) respectively.
Panel (b) carries the only explicit phase label in the figure: 'Cr7C3', written twice, each with a white circle/arrow pointing to a grain-boundary particle in S1000.

Panel (c) labels the near-surface crack path of S1050 as 'Straight cracking' with a red dashed line, and separately marks 'Crack deflection' (white arrow) and 'Across the twins' (yellow dashed arrows).
Panel (f) labels the MHT crack path as 'Zigzag cracking' with a red dashed line, together with 'Crack deflection' (white arrow) and 'Across the twins' (yellow dashed lines).
Panels (d) and (f) mark repeated 'Across the twins' yellow dashed lines, i.e. the crack path crosses interior twin boundaries rather than following only high-angle grain boundaries.

Panel (a) uses orange dashed outlines to highlight connected micropores/crack segments lying along grain boundaries near the fracture surface of S1000, and a white dashed box that indicates a region shown at higher magnification in a companion panel.

Panel (e) is the lowest-magnification view (20 µm scale bar) and shows a comparatively clean MHT matrix with sparse isolated round pores, contrasting with the boundary-connected porosity outlined in panel (a).

The citing text states that Cr7C3 at the grain boundaries in S1000 caused preferential nucleation of cracks at grain boundaries and that the cracks generally follow the RHAGBs under further deformation.

The citing text states that in S1050 removal of intergranular precipitates allows grains to grow and special boundaries to interfere with RHAGBs, so intergranular cracks propagate along special boundaries (yellow dashed lines, Fig. 8(c)) or are deflected (Fig. 8(d)), producing a hybrid intergranular + transgranular ductile fracture.

The citing text states that MHT has more special boundaries and larger grains than S1050, so the crack path constantly crosses and is deflected by special boundaries (Fig. 8(e, f)), increasing the effective crack length and energy dissipation, giving a 29 % increase in impact toughness.

The citing text contrasts the 'straight crack path in S1050' (red dashed line, Fig. 8(c)) with the constantly deflected crack paths in MHT, confirming that the annotated crack-path geometry is the intended comparison of this figure.

The citing text grounds the S1000 crack nucleation in the aggregated micropores at the grain boundaries reported in Fig. 5(a), linking the orange-outlined boundary voids in panel (a) to the earlier fracture-surface observation.

subfigures.description: SEM cross-section of S1000 (10 µm scale bar) with orange dashed outlines tracing linked micropores/crack segments along grain boundaries and a white dashed box marking a region of interest at the upper edge.

Higher-magnification SEM of S1000 (5 µm scale bar) with two white circles and arrows labelling second-phase particles as 'Cr7C3' at grain boundaries; a dark crack/fracture region fills the upper left.

SEM cross-section of S1050 (10 µm scale bar) annotated with a red dashed line 'Straight cracking', a white arrow 'Crack deflection' and yellow dashed arrows 'Across the twins'; an orange dashed outline and a white dashed box are also drawn.
Higher-magnification SEM of S1050 (5 µm scale bar) with yellow dashed lines labelled 'Across the twins' following near-vertical twin boundaries adjacent to a grain boundary.

Low-magnification SEM overview of MHT (20 µm scale bar) showing a relatively clean matrix with sparse round pores, a black fracture-surface region at the top and a white dashed box marking the region magnified in a companion panel.

SEM cross-section of MHT (10 µm scale bar) annotated with a red dashed line 'Zigzag cracking', a white arrow 'Crack deflection' and yellow dashed lines 'Across the twins', showing a repeatedly deflected crack path.

unreadable_items: The figure does not state the magnification factor or explicitly identify which panel each white dashed box in (a), (c) and (e) corresponds to; the box-to-magnified-panel correspondence is inferred from the caption's panel grouping only.
No numeric crack-length, energy or grain-size values are printed on any panel; the 29 % toughness increase and grain sizes come from the citing text/abstract, not from the images.
